rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr calls fairness a blessing and etiquette of learning; without fairness, one neither understands nor seeks understanding.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر: من بركة العلم وآدابه الإنصاف فيه، ومن لم ينصف لم يفهم ولم يتفهم

rows.speaker: مالك ابن أنس
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Anas said fairness was exceptionally scarce in his own era.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن وهب يقول سمعت مالك ابن أنس يقول: ما في زماننا شيء أقل من الإنصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the present is worse: corruption is widespread, and many seek knowledge for status and to defeat rivals in disputation, hardening hearts and undermining piety.
rows.anchor: قلت: هذا في زمن مالك فكيف في زماننا اليوم الذي عم فينا الفساد وكثر فيه الطغام

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When ʿUmar proposed capping dowries at forty ūqiyyas and placing any excess in the treasury, a woman cited 4:20; he admitted she was right and he was wrong.
rows.anchor: أين هذا مما روي عن عمر رضي الله عنه وقد قال: لا تزيدوا في مهور النساء على أربعين أوقية

rows.speaker: امرأة
rows.claim: A woman challenged ʿUmar's proposed dowry cap by citing the Qurʾānic allowance of a large dowry; he accepted her correction.
rows.anchor: فقامت امرأة من صوب النساء طويلة فيها فطس فقالت: ما ذلك لك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A man corrected ʿAlī on a question; ʿAlī accepted the correction and said that above every learned person is someone more learned.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال: سأل رجل عليا رضي الله عنه عن مسألة فقال فيها

rows.speaker: قاسم بن أصبغ
rows.claim: Qāsim ibn Aṣbagh recounts that Bakkār ibn Ḥammād accepted a correction: the report says مجتابي النمار, referring to people wearing front-slit garments, not مجتابي الثمار.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو محمد قاسم بن أصبغ قال: لما رحلت إلى المشرق نزلت القيروان فأخذت على بكر بن حماد حديث مسدد

rows.speaker: يزيد بن الوليد بن عبد الملك
rows.claim: Yazīd ibn al-Walīd's poem advises speaking only within one's knowledge and falling silent when knowledge is exhausted.
rows.anchor: إذا ما تحدثت في مجلس تناهى حديثي إلى ما علمت ولم أعد علمي إلى غيره

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh parse سبحانَكَ as an accusative verbal noun conveying I glorify You with glorification.
rows.anchor: «سبحان» منصوب على المصدر عند الخليل وسيبويه، يؤدي عن معنى نسبحك تسبيحا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī instead parses سبحانَكَ as an accusative vocative in an annexed construction.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو منصوب على أنه نداء مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlīm is an intensive form indicating the abundance of what God knows among His creatures.
rows.anchor: و { العليم } فعيل للمبالغة والتكثير في المعلومات في خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of al-Ḥakīm is al-Ḥākim, the judge or ruler, with added intensity in the form.
rows.anchor: و { الحكيم } معناه الحاكم وبينهما مزيد المبالغة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains al-Ḥakīm as the One who makes things firm; on this account it is an attribute of action.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه المحكم ويجيء الحكيم على هذا من صفات الفعل

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: A group derives al-Ḥakīm from preventing corruption, as a bridle-bit restrains a horse from wandering without purpose.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: «الحكيم» المانع من الفساد ومنه سميت حكمة اللجام لأنها تمنع الفرس

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jareer supplies poetic evidence for restraining: he urges the Banū Ḥanīfa to restrain their foolish people.
rows.anchor: قال جرير: أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr uses أحكمت for fastening reins made of hide and hemp, supporting the sense of making firm or restraining.
rows.anchor: وقال زهير: القائد الخيل منكوبا دوابرها قد أحكمت حكمات القد والأبقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs use أحكم اليتيم to mean restrain him; a well-secured sūra is protected against alteration, and wisdom restrains its possessor from ignorance.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: أحكم اليتيم عن كذا وكذا يريدون منعه. والسورة المحكمة: الممنوعة من التغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحكم means to perfect something and keep it from departing its intended course; مُحْكَم and حَكِيم are intensive forms.
rows.anchor: ويقال: أحكم الشيء إذا أتقنه ومنعه من الخروج عما يريد. فهو محكم وحكيم على التكثير

none: A bare citation of the verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke directed, in the commentators' account, at Jewish scholars.
rows.anchor: هذا استفهام معناه التوبيخ، والمراد في قول أهل التأويل علماء اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jews in Medina told Muslim relatives and in-laws to remain in their faith, conceding that Muḥammad's command was true, while not following it themselves.
rows.anchor: كان يهود المدينة يقول الرجل منهم لصهره ولذي قرابته ولمن بينه وبينه رضاع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another account from Ibn ʿAbbās, rabbis urged their followers to follow the Torah while themselves rejecting its description of Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: كان الأحبار يأمرون مقلديهم وأتباعهم باتباع التوراة، وكانوا يخالفونها في جحدهم صفة محمد

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the rabbis encouraged obedience to God while committing sins themselves.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان الأحبار يحضون على طاعة الله وكانوا هم يواقعون المعاصي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says they encouraged charity while being miserly; al-Qurṭubī says these explanations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: كانوا يحضون على الصدقة ويبخلون. والمعنى متقارب

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارات
rows.claim: Some allusive interpreters understand the rebuke as demanding inward realities from others while contradicting one's own outward forms.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارات: المعنى أتطالبون الناس بحقائق المعاني وأنتم تخالفون عن ظواهر رسومها

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that on the Night Journey the Prophet saw worldly preachers' lips cut with fiery shears; Gabriel identified them as those who commanded righteousness but forgot themselves despite reciting scripture.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Umāma depicts people who preached good but forgot themselves dragging their intestines through Hell and identifying themselves as such preachers.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls the Abū Umāma report weak because al-Ḥuṣayb ibn Jaḥdar was considered weak by Aḥmad and Ibn Maʿīn; Ibn Maʿīn considered Abū Ghālib sound in hadith.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا الحديث وإن كان فيه لين لأن في سنده الخصيب بن جحدر كان الإمام أحمد يستضعفه

rows.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the meaning is transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from Usāma ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: فقد رواه مسلم في صحيحه بمعناه عن أسامة بن زيد قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
rows.claim: Muslim transmits from Usāma ibn Zayd a sound report of a man whose entrails spill into the Fire; he circles like a donkey at a mill and admits preaching what he did not practice.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل يوم القيامة فيلقى في النار فتندلق أقتاب بطنه فيدور بها كما يدور الحمار بالرحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣab means intestine, its plural aqṣāb; aqṭāb is the plural of qitb, also an intestine; tandaliq means to emerge quickly, and another transmitted wording is تنفلق.
rows.anchor: القصب بضم القاف: المعى، وجمعه أقصاب. والأقتاب: الأمعاء، واحدها قتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound report and verse show that a knowledgeable person who fails to do good or avoid wrong is punished more severely than an ignorant person, as one who disregards God's commands and gains no benefit from knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقد دل الحديث الصحيح وألفاظ الآية على أن عقوبة من كان عالما بالمعروف وبالمنكر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī cites the report that the most severely punished on Judgment Day is a learned person whose knowledge did not benefit him, and attributes it to Ibn Mājah.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke concerns failing to practice righteousness, not the act of commanding righteousness itself.
rows.anchor: أن التوبيخ في الآية بسبب ترك فعل البر لا بسبب الأمر بالبر

rows.speaker: منصور الفقيه
rows.claim: Manṣūr al-Faqīh's poem calls those who command what they do not practice mad, unless they are literally struck by madness.
rows.anchor:
وقال منصور الفقيه فأحسن:
إن قوما يأمرونا

rows.speaker: أبو العتاهية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAtāhiya's poem rebukes one who describes piety while the stench of sins rises from his clothes.
rows.anchor:
وقال أبو العتاهية:
وصفت التقى حتى كأنك ذو تقى

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
rows.claim: Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī says not to forbid a trait while practicing it; begin by correcting yourself so counsel is accepted and useful.
rows.anchor:
وقال أبو الأسود الدؤلي:
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن مطر
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn Maṭar recounts that Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḥīrī answered a request to speak with a poem comparing an ungodly preacher to a sick doctor treating patients.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن مطر: حضرت مجلس أبي عثمان الحيري الزاهد فخرج وقعد على موضعه

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان الحيري
rows.claim: After Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḥīrī's poem, the audience broke into weeping and commotion.
rows.anchor: قال: فارتفعت الأصوات بالبكاء والضجيج

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī disliked admonitory storytelling, citing this verse, 61:2, and Shuʿayb's words in 11:88.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم النخعي: إني لأكره القصص لثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: سلم بن عمرو
rows.claim: Salm ibn ʿAmr's poem mocks a preacher who renounces worldly life for listeners while seeking their support and not living by his advice.
rows.anchor: وقال سلم بن عمرو: ما أقبح التزهيد من واعظ يزهد الناس ولا يزهد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: When al-Ḥasan told Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh to counsel his companions and Muṭarrif feared saying what he did not do, al-Ḥasan replied that nobody does all he says; refusing to counsel would please Satan.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن لمطرف بن عبد الله: عظ أصحابك فقال إني أخاف أن أقول ما لا أفعل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says that if people could enjoin right and forbid wrong only when faultless, nobody would do so; Mālik agreed that everyone has some fault.
rows.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول: لو كان المرء لا يأمر بالمعروف ولا ينهى عن المنكر حتى لا يكون فيه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-birr can mean obedience and good action, truthfulness, a fox's cub, or driving sheep; a cited idiom contrasts calling sheep with driving them, and poetry uses it for obedience.
rows.anchor: البر هنا الطاعة والعمل الصالح. والبر: الصدق. والبر: ولد الثعلب. والبر: سوق الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In another poetic usage al-birr means the heart; with ḍamma it is familiar, while with fatḥa it denotes honoring and reverence, as in a dutiful child.
rows.anchor:
ويقال: إن البر الفؤاد في قوله:
أكون مكان البر منه ودونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here forgetting means leaving or neglecting; the same sense appears in 9:67, 6:44, and 2:237. The word can also mean the opposite of remembering or retaining.
rows.anchor: والنسيان بكسر النون يكون بمعنى الترك وهو المراد هنا، وفي قوله تعالى: نسوا الله فنسيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says Adam forgot, and his descendants consequently forget; al-Qurṭubī says the report will be discussed later.
rows.anchor: " نسي آدم فنسيت ذريته "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī gives نسيان as the verbal noun and cautions against vocalizing it as nisayān, associating that form with the dual of nisāʾ, a vein.
rows.anchor: وقد نسيت الشيء نسيانا، ولا تقل نسيانا بالتحريك لأن النسيان إنما هو تثنية نسا العرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anfus is a broken plural of nafs and is classified as a plural of paucity.
rows.anchor: وأنفس: جمع نفس، جمع قلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs can mean spirit; al-Qurṭubī cites 39:42 and reports from Bilāl and the Prophet as evidence that the plural there means souls.
rows.anchor: ومن الدليل على أن النفس الروح قوله تعالى: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

rows.speaker: بلال
rows.claim: In a report from Ibn Shihāb, Bilāl tells the Prophet that what took his soul had taken the Prophet's soul too.
rows.anchor: في قول بلال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث ابن شهاب

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Mālik from Zayd ibn Aslam has the Prophet say that God took their spirits and could have returned them at another time.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام في حديث زيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Nafs can also mean blood, as in poetry about blood flowing on sword edges.
rows.anchor:
والنفس أيضا الدم يقال: سالت نفسه قال الشاعر:
تسيل على حد السيوف نفوسنا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī holds that an animal without flowing blood does not make water impure if it dies in it.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: ما ليس له نفس سائلة فإنه لا ينجس الماء إذا مات فيه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: Nafs may also mean the body; a poem describes the body or blood of al-Mundhir being brought into his house.
rows.anchor:
والنفس أيضا الجسد قال الشاعر:
نبئت أن بني سحيم أدخلوا أبياتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Book makes the rebuke especially forceful; the Book is the Torah, and anyone acting in the same way shares their censure.
rows.anchor: السابعة: قوله تعالى: { وأنتم تتلون الكتاب } توبيخ عظيم لمن فهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilāwa means reading, originally derived from following words in sequence; the root also has other senses such as leaving, remainder, preserving, pursuing a due, and nearing death.
rows.anchor: وأصل التلاوة الاتباع، ولذلك استعمل في القراءة لأنه يتبع بعض الكلام ببعض في حروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks why they do not restrain themselves from this ruinous behavior; ʿaql means restraint, as a camel's ʿiqāl prevents movement.
rows.anchor: الثامنة: قوله تعالى: { أفلا تعقلون } أي أفلا تمنعون أنفسكم من مواقعة هذه الحال المردية لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blood compensation is called ʿaql because it restrains a victim's guardian from killing the offender; the word also describes restraint of the stomach and tongue and a fortified person.
rows.anchor: ومنه العقل للدية لأنه يمنع ولي المقتول عن قتل الجاني. ومنه اعتقال البطن واللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿaql can also mean a red textile used by Arab women to cover howdahs; the verse introducing ʿAlqama's poetic evidence appears here.
rows.anchor: والعقل: ثوب أحمر تتخذه نساء العرب تغشى به الهوادج قال علقمة

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama's verse calls a red textile عقل and contrasts it with رقم; المدموم means red here, though it can also mean a camel full of fat, and the terms name two kinds of cloth.
rows.anchor: عقلا ورقما تكاد الطير تخطفه كأنه من دم الأجواف مدموم

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Fāris says ʿaql is a textile pattern running lengthwise, whereas raqm is a round pattern.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس: والعقل من شيات الثياب ما كان نقشه طولا وما كان نقشه مستديرا فهو الرقم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a rational person acts on what God obligates; someone who does not act accordingly is ignorant.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: العاقل من عمل بما أوجب الله عليه، فمن لم يعمل فهو جاهل

rows.speaker: أهل الحق
rows.claim: The people of truth agree that reason exists and is created: if nonexistent it could not distinguish some beings, and if eternal it would rival God's eternity.
rows.anchor: اتفق أهل الحق على أن العقل كائن موجود ليس بقديم ولا معدوم

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers hold reason to be eternal; some call it a subtle substance in the body emitting a ray that distinguishes truths, while others call it a simple substance.
rows.anchor: وقد صارت الفلاسفة إلى أن العقل قديم ثم منهم من صار إلى جوهر لطيف في البدن

rows.speaker: طائفة من الفلاسفة
rows.claim: One philosophical group locates reason in the brain as the seat of sensation; another locates it in the heart as the source of life and the senses.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة منهم: محله الدماغ لأن الدماغ محل الحس. وقالت طائفة أخرى: محله القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rejects reason as a substance: substances are alike, so if one substance were reason, every substance would have to be reason.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول في العقل بأنه جوهر فاسد، من حيث إن الجواهر متماثلة فلو كان جوهر عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining reason as perceiving realities is closer than the substance theories but still wrong, since perception belongs to the living, whereas reason is an accident unable itself to perceive or desire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن العقل هو المدرك للأشياء على ما هي عليه من حقائق المعاني. وهذا القول وإن كان أقرب

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري وأبو إسحاق الإسفرايني
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿarī, al-Isfarāyīnī, and other authorities define reason as knowledge, since one cannot reason without knowing or know without reasoning.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري والأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني وغيرهما من المحققين: العقل هو العلم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr defines reason as necessary knowledge of what is obligatory, possible, and impossible; Abū al-Maʿālī chose this in al-Irshād but in al-Burhān chose a capacity for acquiring knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر: العقل علوم ضرورية بوجوب الواجبات وجواز الجائزات واستحالة المستحيلات

rows.speaker: المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī is reported to define reason as an innate disposition; the author notes that the judge's position is challenged and its error argued in al-Burhān.
rows.anchor: وحكي في البرهان عن المحاسبي أنه قال: العقل غريزة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وابن مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Ibn Mujāhid are reported to call reason an instrument of discrimination; al-Qalānisī calls it a discriminating faculty, and al-Muḥāsibī calls it lights and insights.
rows.anchor: وحكى الأستاذ أبو بكر عن الشافعي وأبي عبد الله بن مجاهد أنهما قالا: العقل آلة التمييز

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Ustadh Abū Bakr doubts that al-Shāfiʿī and Ibn Mujāhid used the phrase instrument of discrimination; applying an instrument to an accident is metaphorical, and the other definitions are loose expressions.
rows.anchor: والأولى ألا يصح هذا النقل عن الشافعي ولا عن ابن مجاهد، فإن الآلة إنما تستعمل في الآلة المثبتة

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Ustadh Abū Bakr concludes that reason is neither a form nor a light but a means by which lights and insights are gained; al-Qurṭubī promises further discussion at the sūra's verse of divine unity.
rows.anchor: والعقل ليس بصورة ولا نور، ولكن تستفاد به الأنوار والبصائر. وسيأتي في هذه السورة بيان فائدته في آية التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مَن is the subject, أظلم its predicate, and the sense is that no one is more unjust.
rows.anchor: «من» رفع بالابتداء، و { أظلم } خبره والمعنى لا أحد أظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause أن يذكر is parsed as an accusative apposition to مساجد; alternatives posit an omitted sense of aversion or a deleted preposition من.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير: كراهية أن يذكر، ثم حذف. ويجوز أن يكون التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the mosques as the Temple in Jerusalem and its prayer niches; others identify them as the Kaʿba or all mosques, with the Kaʿba pluralized because it is their qibla or for honor.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالمساجد هنا بيت المقدس ومحاريبه. وقيل الكعبة، وجمعت لأنها قبلة المساجد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the usual kasra in masjid against the general fatḥa pattern of nouns and verbal nouns from this verb class; some Arabs use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول: مسجد، بفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, masjad can mean the mark on a man's forehead from prostration; al-Jawharī calls the seven bodily points of prostration the ārāb.
rows.anchor: والمسجد بالفتح: جبهة الرجل حيث يصيبه ندب السجود. والآراب: السبعة مساجد قاله الجوهري

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators report that the verse was revealed about Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: فذكر المفسرون أنها نزلت في بخت نصر لأنه كان أخرب بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say the verse concerns Christians: despite honoring the Temple, they ruined it and barred worshippers in hostility toward Jews.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: نزلت في النصارى والمعنى كيف تدعون أيها النصارى أنكم من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that Christian hatred of Jews led them to aid the Babylonian Magian Nebuchadnezzar in destroying the Temple; the destruction reportedly lasted until ʿUmar's time.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة قال: أولئك أعداء الله النصارى، حملهم إبغاض اليهود على أن أعانوا بخت نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account places the verse among polytheists who barred the Prophet and Muslims from the Sacred Mosque at al-Ḥudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في المشركين إذ منعوا المصلين والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وصدوهم عن المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers the general reading: it covers anyone who prevents worship in any mosque until the Resurrection; restricting it to particular people and mosques is weak because the wording is general and plural.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد من منع من كل مسجد إلى يوم القيامة، وهو الصحيح لأن اللفظ عام ورد بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosque destruction can be literal, as in the accounts of Nebuchadnezzar and the Christians, or figurative: blocking prayer and public Islamic rites ruins a mosque.
rows.anchor: خراب المساجد قد يكون حقيقيا كتخريب بخت نصر والنصارى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: الغزنوي
rows.claim: Al-Ghaznawī names the Roman ruler in an account of the attack as Naṭūs ibn Isbiyāsiyānūs; the attackers killed and captured people, burned the Torah, defiled the Temple, and ruined it.
rows.anchor: قيل: اسمه نطوس ابن اسبيسانوس الرومي فيما ذكر الغزنوي فقتلوا وسبوا، وحرقوا التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mosque built beside another to split its congregation and cause discord may be prohibited and demolished; this is an exception to the general permission to build mosques.
rows.anchor: ولا يمنع بناء المساجد إلا أن يقصدوا الشقاق والخلاف، بأن يبنوا مسجدا إلى جنب مسجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed people not to prevent God's female servants from attending His mosques.
rows.anchor: " لا تمنعوا إماء الله مساجد الله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mosque may not be demolished, sold, or deactivated even if its neighborhood is abandoned; a nearby mosque intended to divide the congregation and ruin the first may be prohibited and demolished.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز نقض المسجد ولا بيعه ولا تعطيله وإن خربت المحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī further holds that a town should not have two congregational mosques, one mosque two imams, or two congregational groups praying in one mosque.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون في المصر جامعان، ولا لمسجد واحد إمامان، ولا يصلي في مسجد جماعتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows the gravity of prayer: since prayer is the best deed and greatest in reward, preventing it is a grave sin.
rows.anchor: ودلت الآية أيضا على تعظيم أمر الصلاة، وأنها لما كانت أفضل الأعمال وأعظمها أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any place where God can be worshipped and prostration performed is called a mosque; the Prophet said the earth was made a place of prayer and purification.
rows.anchor: كل موضع يمكن أن يعبد الله فيه ويسجد له يسمى مسجدا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees that a place explicitly designated for prayer ceases to be private property and becomes common to Muslims; a home prayer room remains private if reserved, but becomes a public mosque if opened to everyone.
rows.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة على أن البقعة إذا عينت للصلاة بالقول خرجت عن جملة الأملاك المختصة بربها

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولئك is the subject, what follows is its predicate, and خائفين is a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: حال يعنى إذا استولى عليها المسلمون وحصلت تحت سلطانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once Muslims govern the mosques, an unbeliever can enter only fearing expulsion and discipline; al-Qurṭubī takes the verse as evidence that unbelievers may not enter a mosque.
rows.anchor: يعنى إذا استولى عليها المسلمون وحصلت تحت سلطانهم فلا يتمكن الكافر حينئذ من دخولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Christian interpretation, a report says Christians could not enter Jerusalem's Temple after ʿUmar rebuilt it under Islam without being harshly beaten.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل الآية في النصارى روى أنه مر زمان بعد بناء عمر بيت المقدس في الإسلام لا يدخله نصراني إلا أوجع ضربا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: On the Quraysh interpretation, the Prophet ordered a proclamation that after that year no polytheist would perform pilgrimage and no naked person would circumambulate the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: " ألا لا يحج بعد العام مشرك، ولا يطوف بالبيت عريان "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation treats the statement as declarative in form but imperative in purpose: fight them until none enters the Sacred Mosque except in fear, like the prohibition phrased as a report in 33:53.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو خبر ومقصوده الأمر أي جاهدوهم واستأصلوهم حتى لا يدخل أحد منهم المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says worldly disgrace means killing for a belligerent unbeliever and the jizya for a protected non-Muslim.
rows.anchor: قيل القتل للحربي، والجزية للذمي عن قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies worldly disgrace with the Mahdī's rise and the conquest of Amorium, Rome, Constantinople, and other cities.
rows.anchor: السدي: الخزي لهم في الدنيا قيام المهدي، وفتح عمورية ورومية وقسطنطينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Quraysh interpretation, disgrace came with the conquest, while the afterlife punishment applies to those who died as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ومن جعلها في قريش جعل الخزي عليهم في الفتح، والعذاب في الآخرة لمن مات منهم كافرا

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scholars say this verse was revealed before 2:142, although it appears after it in the sūra.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء: هذه الآية مقدمة في النزول على قوله تعالى: سيقول السفهآء من الناس

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the Prophet's turning his face as turning it toward the sky; al-Zajjāj says he turned his eyes to gaze upward, a similar sense.
rows.anchor: تحول وجهك إلى السماء قاله الطبري. الزجاج: تقلب عينيك في النظر إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is singled out because things associated with it are held in special reverence and come from it, such as rain, mercy, and revelation.
rows.anchor: وخص السماء بالذكر إذ هي مختصة بتعظيم ما أضيف إليها ويعود منها كالمطر والرحمة والوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarḍāhā means that you love or desire it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ترضاها } تحبها

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says that while praying toward Jerusalem, the Prophet raised his head toward the sky awaiting an instruction because he wished to pray toward the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: كان إذا صلى نحو بيت المقدس رفع رأسه إلى السماء ينظر ما يؤمر به

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months and wished to face the Kaʿba before this revelation.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو إسحق عن البراء قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to turn one's face toward the Sacred Mosque means toward the Kaʿba, with no disagreement on that point.
rows.anchor: يعني الكعبة، ولا خلاف في هذا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the direction is aligned with the whole House; Ibn ʿUmar says it is aligned with the Kaʿba's rainspout, as reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
rows.anchor: قيل: حيال البيت كله عن ابن عباس. وقال ابن عمر: حيال الميزاب من الكعبة قاله ابن عطية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ says the Kaʿba is the direction for the mosque, the mosque for the sanctuary, and the sanctuary for people across the earth.
rows.anchor: روى ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatr means direction or side here and functions as a locative adverb, like toward or opposite; it is accusative as an adjunct where the action occurs.
rows.anchor: الشطر له محامل: يكون الناحية والجهة، كما في هذه الآية، وهو ظرف مكان

rows.speaker: داود بن أبي هند
rows.claim: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind says Ibn Masʿūd's codex read تلقاء المسجد الحرام in place of شطر المسجد الحرام.
rows.anchor: وقال داود بن أبي هند: إن في حرف ابن مسعود «فول وجهك تلقاء المسجد الحرام»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited anonymous poetic lines use shatr for a direction or destination, including toward Banū Tamīm and toward a fortress; another says a message sent toward ʿAmr does not suffice.
rows.anchor:
أقول لأم زنباع أقيمي
صدور العيش شطر بني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatr also means half, as in the prophetic saying that purification is half of faith.
rows.anchor:
وشطر الشيء: نصفه ومنه الحديث:
" الطهور شطر الإيمان "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb shatara can mean to approach in one construction and turn away in another; shāṭir is named for departing from the straight way, with a reported gloss of distancing oneself from God's prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ويكون من الأضداد، يقال: شطر إلى كذا إذا أقبل نحوه، وشطر عن كذا إذا أبعد منه

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Scholars agree that the Kaʿba is the qibla in every region; anyone who sees it and knows its direction must face it, and prayer performed while knowingly facing away must be repeated.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف بين العلماء أن الكعبة قبلة في كل أفق، وأجمعوا على أن من شاهدها وعاينها
